items.title: Protest shuts Obollo-Afor market over alleged selective haulage tax
items.description: By Dennis Agbo ENUGU — Commercial activities were disrupted at Obollo-Afor Market in Udenu Local Government Area of Enugu State on Wednesday as traders shut their shops and protested against what they described as selective collection of a N25,000 haulage levy on trucks loading and offloading goods at the market. The traders, who carried placards with various inscriptions, marched to the Udenu Local Government secretariat to present their grievances to council officials. They alleged that the Enugu State Internal Revenue Service (ESIRS) had singled out Obollo-Afor Market for the collection of the haulage levy, claiming that similar charges were not being imposed at other markets in the state. However, the Chairman of ESIRS, Mr Emmanuel Nnamani, in a letter to the traders, explained that the haulage levy was not payable by traders buying or selling goods in markets. According to him, the levy applies strictly to truck drivers operating on interstate routes. Speaking at the council secretariat, Chairman of the Obollo-Afor Market Traders Association, Mr Charles Eze, said the alleged levy had discouraged truck operators from bringing goods to the market. Eze said some truck owners had diverted their consignments to Orba, Enugu-Ezike, Nsukka and Orie-Igboeze, allegedly because they were not required to pay similar charges at those locations. “The truck owners have diverted our goods to Orba, Enugu-Ezike, Nsukka and Orie-Igboeze, asking us to come and pick our goods there because they don’t pay such levies there except in Obollo-Afor. And so we are asking, why Obollo alone?” he asked. Eze said traders had no objection to the state’s e-ticketing system, which he said they had been complying with, but described the alleged selective haulage levy as unfair. He said the development had resulted in a decline in the flow of goods to the market for more than two months. According to him, traders had attempted to engage the revenue service over the matter but were yet to reach a resolution. “This is the reason we closed shops for protest because truck operators bringing goods for us have refused to come to Obollo-Afor and it has crumbled the Obollo-Afor market and hunger has set in,” he said. Eze appealed to Governor Peter Mbah to intervene, stressing that traders were not opposed to paying legitimate taxes and levies. “We are not saying that we won’t pay levies, but let it be fees that are equally obtained in other places. We are ready to pay any amount of levy that is obtained in Akwata, Ogbete, Nsukka, Orba or in any other market in the state, but let Obollo-Afor not be an exception or singled out for selective taxation,” he said. Other market leaders who participated in the protest, including Chief James Odo of the Foodstuff Dealers Association and Chief Damian Nwodo of the Electrical and Electronics Dealers Association, also expressed concern over the impact of the levy on their businesses. Responding on behalf of the Udenu Local Government Council, its Secretary, Mr Chika Aroh, said the council had scheduled a meeting with representatives of ESIRS to clarify whether the levy was being collected only in Obollo-Afor. Aroh said the council would communicate its findings to the traders after the meeting. “But for now, we will tell them to stop the collection. After the Thursday meeting, we will communicate with you. Our promise is that we will remedy the matter,” he said. The post Protest shuts Obollo-Afor market over alleged selective haulage tax appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: ‘Huge hug to you’, Ronaldo sends message to grieving Messi
items.description: By Emmanuel Okogba Portuguese superstar Cristiano Ronaldo has sent a heartfelt message of support to Lionel Messi following the death of the Argentine’s father, Jorge Messi. As reported by Fabrizio Romano on X on Wednesday, Ronaldo wrote: “Huge hug to you and your loved ones in this difficult moment, Leo. Stay strong.” The message comes days after Messi bid farewell to his father, who passed away at the age of 68 after a battle with cancer. Jorge Messi had been a central figure in his son’s life and career, serving as his agent and emotional anchor since childhood. In a social media post on Wednesday, the 39-year-old Inter Miami forward expressed deep grief and revealed he has “serious doubts” about continuing to play football for much longer. “I don’t know what I’ll do without you, I don’t know how to go on. I just played football, and now I have serious doubts about continuing to do so for much longer,” Messi wrote. He reflected on his father’s absence during the 2026 World Cup, noting that Jorge’s health had deteriorated just days before the tournament began. Messi said he had hoped to reach the final so his father could travel to watch, but Jorge was unable to attend. Argentina reached the final but lost 1-0 to Spain in New Jersey. Messi scored eight goals during the tournament. He returned to the United States on Tuesday night after attending a private funeral on Sunday in Perez, near Rosario, with close family and a few Argentina teammates. Messi described his father as “a father, a friend, and an agent” who “never put a foot wrong.” Jorge Messi left his job and family in Argentina in 2000 to accompany the then-13-year-old Lionel to Barcelona for treatment of a growth hormone deficiency and to support his early career. Despite their long-standing rivalry on the pitch, Ronaldo’s message has been widely noted as another example of the mutual respect between the two football icons. The post ‘Huge hug to you’, Ronaldo sends message to grieving Messi appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Oudalan/Environnement: 1 000 plants mis en terre pour lancer la campagne nationale de reforestation
items.description: Burkina-Oudalan-Environnement-Reforestation-Lancement Oudalan/Environnement: 1 000 plants mis en terre pour lancer la campagne nationale de reforestation Gorom-Gorom, 11 août 2026 (AIB) – La campagne nationale de reforestation 2026 a été officiellement lancée mardi dans la province de l’Oudalan par la Direction provinciale de l’Environnement et de l’Eau, sous la présidence du haut-commissaire de la province, Valentin Maré, à travers la mise en terre de 1 000 plants dans le bosquet provincial. L’activité a mobilisé les autorités administratives, les Forces de défense et de sécurité (FDS), les collectivités territoriales et les organisations de la société civile. Prenant la parole, le deuxième vice-président de la délégation spéciale de la commune de Gorom-Gorom, Hamadou Boureima, a rappelé l’importance de l’arbre dans la préservation de l’environnement. « L’arbre, c’est la vie », a-t-il déclaré, invitant les populations à planter et à entretenir davantage d’arbres afin de lutter contre les effets du changement climatique et de contribuer au reverdissement de la province. Le directeur provincial de l’Environnement et de l’Eau, Mohamed Konané, a expliqué que le démarrage tardif de la campagne était notamment lié à la pluviométrie de la zone. Les 1 000 plants mis en terre sont constitués notamment de caïlcédrats, de neem, de baobabs et d’Acacia nilotica. L’activité a également permis d’amorcer la mise en place d’un bosquet de plantes médicinales, conformément à l’initiative « Une province, un bosquet de plantes médicinales », lancée en 2025 par le président du Faso, le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré. Dans son discours d’ouverture, le haut-commissaire de l’Oudalan, Valentin Maré, a salué l’engagement des populations et des différents acteurs en faveur de la restauration du couvert végétal. Il a appelé les différentes couches socioprofessionnelles à créer des « micros-écosystèmes », dont l’ensemble contribuera à réduire les effets du changement climatique. Après une démonstration pratique de plantation, le haut-commissaire a procédé à la mise en terre du premier plant, donnant ainsi le coup d’envoi aux travaux de reboisement. Les participants ont ensuite poursuivi la plantation et l’arrosage des plants dans le bosquet provincial, intégré à la forêt communale, qui s’étend sur une superficie clôturée de 2,70 hectares. Cette mobilisation traduit la volonté des acteurs de l’Oudalan de faire de la restauration des écosystèmes une responsabilité collective et un levier durable de résilience face aux défis climatiques. Agence d’information du Burkina DAM/bak

items.title: Kufuor urges political actors to protect Ghana’s democratic institutions
items.description: Former President John Agyekum Kufuor has urged political actors to protect Ghana’s democratic institutions and avoid treating electoral victories as ownership of the state. He said institutions including Parliament, the judiciary, the media and other independent constitutional bodies must be allowed to operate effectively to safeguard democracy, accountability and the rule of law. Mr Kufuor, Life Patron of the Busia Institute, made the call at the 2026 Busia Institute Lecture in London, held on the theme, “Centre-Right Political Thought in Africa: The Ghanaian Experience.” “An opponent remains a fellow citizen, and a temporary majority does not own the republic,” Mr Kufuor said. He said Ghana’s centre-right political tradition had historically been rooted in constitutional government, liberty under the law, a free press, private enterprise, social responsibility and decentralisation. Mr Kufuor stressed that strong institutions were essential to preventing the abuse of political power and ensuring that democratic governance remained responsive to citizens. His comments formed part of discussions on the relevance of Ghana’s political traditions and their contribution to the country’s democratic and socio-economic development. The lecture, held at the London Hilton on Park Lane, was the first Busia Institute Lecture to be organised outside Ghana and brought together diplomats, Members of Parliament, Ghanaian professionals, members of the diaspora and other guests. The event also featured a screening of the documentary *Busia in His Own Words* and a photographic exhibition showcasing historical materials from the period of Professor Kofi Abrefa Busia’s government.

The tour, which continues on Thursday, forms part of the President’s post-election appreciation engagements with Ghanaians following his victory in the 2024 general elections. President Mahama is expected to engage citizens and stakeholders in the Upper East Region while advancing his government’s national reset agenda. The Presidency says the tour provides an opportunity for the President to interact directly with communities, listen to their concerns and discuss the government’s development priorities. The Upper East leg is the latest in a series of regional engagements under the Resetting Ghana Tour. A post announcing the visit said President Mahama would spend Thursday and Friday in the region for the latest instalment of the tour. The tour is also expected to provide a platform for citizens, traditional leaders, community groups and other stakeholders to raise issues affecting the region and seek government intervention. The Upper East Region played a significant role in Mahama’s 2024 electoral victory, with the National Democratic Congress candidate securing more than 360,000 presidential votes in the region.

items.title: Judges can hear substantive cases during legal vacation if lawyers have no objection – Tuah-Yeboah
items.description: Former Deputy Attorney General Alfred Tuah-Yeboah has explained that judges can hear substantive cases during legal vacation, but said lawyers involved in such cases must first be consulted and have no objection to the arrangement. His comments come amid a growing debate over the decision to allow selected cases to proceed during the current legal vacation, particularly proceedings involving former National Signals Bureau (NSB) Director-General Kwabena Adu-Boahen and former National Food and Buffer Stock Company (NAFCO) Chief Executive Officer Hanan Abdul-Wahab. Speaking on JoyNews’ The Pulse, Mr Tuah-Yeboah said the practice of having judges sit during legal vacation predates Ghana’s independence and is intended primarily to deal with urgent matters. He explained that vacation judges traditionally handle applications such as bail, injunctions, probate, letters of administration and other urgent proceedings rather than substantive trials involving the taking of evidence and cross-examination of witnesses. According to him, however, there is an established procedure where a judge wishes to hear a substantive matter during the vacation. “Vacation judges have not been [hearing] substantive matters, that is, taking evidence and then allowing counsel to cross-examine witnesses,” he explained on Wednesday, August 12. Mr Tuah-Yeboah said where a judge intends to proceed with a substantive case during the vacation, the lawyers involved are normally consulted. “If a vacation judge is minded to hear substantive matters during vacation, the lawyers in the matter are always consulted, and if they have no objection, then a warrant is secured, and then the matter is heard during legal vacation,” he said. He therefore identified the absence of consultation with lawyers as the key concern in the current controversy. “In this particular instance, we are told that the lawyers were not involved in the decision to hear the matter during the legal vacation. And that’s where the problem is,” he said. Mr Tuah-Yeboah stressed that his position does not challenge the authority of the Chief Justice to authorise judges to sit during the legal vacation. Rather, he argued that the established practice requires the lawyers involved in substantive cases to be part of the decision before such proceedings are scheduled. His comments come as Samuel Atta Akyea, lead counsel for former National Signals Bureau Director, Kwabena Adu-Boahene and wife, was absent in court on Tuesday despite a directive that trial is to continue during the legal vacation. Deputy Attorney General Dr Justice Srem-Sai has argued that lawyers cannot unilaterally refuse to appear before Vacation Courts, maintaining that selected judges have the authority to conduct both interlocutory and substantive proceedings during the period. Mr Tuah-Yeboah’s position, however, is that while substantive hearings can take place during the vacation, the participation and consent of counsel involved form part of the established practice for such hearings.

Fillette insultée : l’influenceur Anouar Sayoud condamné à de la prison
items.description: Le tribunal de Boufarik dans la wilaya de Blida a rendu ce mercredi 12 août son verdict dans l’affaire de l’influenceur Anouar S. qui a tenu des propos insultants envers une fillette de 8 ans. Il a été condamné à deux ans de prison, dont un avec sursis, et à une amende de 200.000 DA, avec l’obligation de verser un dinar symbolique à l’instance nationale de protection de l’enfance. Lors de son procès qui s’est tenu durant ce mois d'août, le procureur de la République a requis trois ans de prison ferme et une amende de 300.000 DA. Anouar Sayoud condamné à deux ans de prison, dont un avec sursis Anouar Sayoud a été arrêté à la suite de la diffusion d’une vidéo sur les réseaux sociaux où il tenait un discours moralisateur à l’égard d’une fillette de 8 ans en raison de sa tenue vestimentaire, allant jusqu’à la qualifier de « prostituée ». Ses propos ont suscité une vive polémique sur les réseaux sociaux entre ceux qui l’ont défendu, comme l’ancien président du MSP Abderrazak Makri, et ceux qui ont exprimé leur indignation, tout en condamnant son acte. Dans un communiqué diffusé lundi 3 août dernier, le parquet de la République près le tribunal de Boufarik a indiqué que Anouar Sayoud est poursuivi pour « des infractions flagrantes de discrimination et d’atteinte à la vie privée de l’enfant par des publications susceptibles de lui nuire », et ce, conformément aux articles 2 et 31 de la loi relative à la prévention et à la lutte contre la discrimination et les discours de haine, et à l’article 140 de la loi relative à la protection de l’enfant. items.title: FACT-CHECK: Abena Osei-Asare’s claim that BoG’s 2025 financial report understates $1.7bn gold trade loss FALSE
items.description: JoyNews Research has fact-checked a claim by Abena Osei-Asare, former Minister of State at the Finance Ministry and Chairperson of Parliament’s Public Accounts Committee (PAC), concerning the losses the Bank of Ghana reported in connection with its Domestic Gold Purchase Programme (DGPP). The claim Speaking in a video widely shared on social media, Abena Osei-Asare said: “according to the IMF, the Domestic Gold Purchase Programme recorded losses to the tune of $1.7 billion, but if you recall, the Bank of Ghana in their 2025 financial statement reported $214 million as the loss. This loss of $1.7 billion is equivalent to GH¢22 billion, and that is 1.5% of our GDP.” This statement was framed to suggest that the Bank of Ghana had understated the losses tied to the DGPP in its published audited accounts. The verdict: FALSE Checks by JoyNews Research indicate the claim does not hold up. It juxtaposes two figures that are not comparable, a full IMF programme estimate against a narrow IMF sub-figure (Q1-Q3 of 2025), and misattributes the smaller number to BoG’s financial statements for the entire 2025. What the Bank actually reported In its 2025 financial statements, the Bank of Ghana reported a net loss on gold deals of approximately GH¢9.1 billion. At the Bank’s end-2025 reference rate of GH¢10.45 to the US dollar, GH¢9.1 billion is roughly $871 million. This comprised a GH¢8.85 billion net loss on Gold for Reserves (G4R) and a GH¢0.20 billion net loss on Gold for Oil (G4O), the latter programme having been discontinued in March 2025. Crucially, the $214 million figure Abena Osei-Asare attributed to BoG’s financial statements for the entire 2025 does not appear there as the reported loss. It is instead an IMF figure covering only part of the year. In its December 2025 review, the Fund stated that “in 2025 through end-Q3, losses from the artisanal and small-scale (ASM) doré gold transactions component of G4R have reached $214 million (0.2 percent of GDP), mostly on trading losses but also on GoldBod off-takers’ fees.” That is a three-quarter, single-component estimate, not the audited full-year loss in BoG’s accounts. On the $1.7 billion / GH¢22 billion figure In a visualized data pack from the Bank of Ghana cited by JoyNews Research , the central bank had indicated that it recorded a “loss on doré gold of ₵21.89 billion” (GROSS) which is equivalent to the GH¢22 billion loss ($1.7 billion) revealed by the IMF in the August 2026 report. This means the apex bank did not understate the gross gold traded losses of 2025 as claimed by the Chairperson of Parliament’s Public Accounts Committee, Abena Osei-Asare.

items.title: AEW–WPC clash exposes Africa’s failure to defend its own energy calendar
items.description: The collision between Cape Town and Riyadh has been blamed on global competition and Saudi convening power. But it also exposes an African weakness: the continent has not built enough collective weight around its own strategic energy calendar. The dispute over African Energy Week and the World Petroleum Congress has been examined largely through the lenses of Saudi influence, competition for ministers and CEOs, investment rivalry and institutional respect. All of those questions matter. But October 2026 also exposes a weakness closer to home. Africa has not yet built enough collective power around its own energy calendar. African Energy Week is scheduled for Cape Town from October 12 to 16, while the 25th WPC Energy Congress will take place in Riyadh from October 11 to 15. Four days of their programmes overlap almost completely. The obvious question is why WPC moved into AEW’s week. The harder question is this: why was it possible to do so without creating an overwhelming institutional obstacle for WPC itself? That question goes to the heart of Africa’s challenge. Important dates become powerful because institutions defend them The global economic calendar contains events that governments, companies and investors treat as almost immovable. Executives reserve the dates, media organisations plan around them, sponsors commit early. Governments schedule delegations’ years in advance. Other organisers think twice before competing directly against them. That status is not created by branding alone. It is created by institutional habit. Africa’s ambition should therefore go beyond making AEW successful. The goal should be to make its strongest continental energy gatherings calendar landmarks that the international industry cannot easily ignore. The WPC clash suggests Africa is not there yet. Africa has events, but not enough calendar power African Energy Week is already a major gathering, with sessions covering investment, upstream development, gas, electricity, local content and country-specific opportunities. But scale does not automatically create calendar power. Calendar power exists when a gathering becomes so deeply embedded in government and corporate planning that competing against it carries a clear cost. That requires more than an organiser. It requires collective ownership of the date. If African petroleum ministries treat AEW as one conference among many, international institutions will do the same. If national oil companies decide attendance only after receiving invitations, the date remains flexible. If senior African officials do not place the event into their official forward calendars, its institutional protection remains weak. And if Africa itself hosts multiple competing energy gatherings chasing the same ministers, sponsors and investors, outsiders will not always know which African event carries strategic priority. African governments hold the real leverage The WPC controversy has often been framed as an issue between conference organisers. That may be too narrow. African governments are the continent’s most important energy stakeholders. Their ministries regulate resources and their national oil companies control assets. Their agencies issue licences and their governments negotiate investment agreements. Collectively, they possess enormous leverage over the international energy-conference market. Imagine if Africa’s major petroleum-producing states formally designated one annual week as a priority continental energy-investment period. Imagine APPO members, national oil companies, regulators and development finance institutions committing senior participation several years ahead. International oil companies would know it; banks would know it and investors would know it. Other conference organisers would know it. A competing global event could still choose those dates, but it would do so knowing exactly what it was competing against. That is how calendar power is built. Fragmentation weakens Africa’s position The continent’s broader problem is fragmentation. Africa’s energy sector is divided across multiple regulatory systems, investment regimes, national priorities and conference platforms. Companies can spend much of the year moving between petroleum conferences, gas forums, mining events, investment summits and country roadshows. Some take place in Africa. Others take African ministers and projects to Europe, the Middle East and North America. Competition between events is not necessarily bad. But excessive fragmentation can dilute bargaining power. The same ministers are invited repeatedly. The same CEOs are pursued. The same sponsors are approached. The same investors are courted. What appears to be a rich ecosystem of events can also become a competition among African platforms for the same limited pool of attention. The WPC clash makes that weakness harder to ignore. Africa still exports too much of its investment diplomacy and there is another contradiction. Africa wants international investors to take African-led platforms seriously, yet governments continue to market many of the continent’s energy opportunities abroad. Roadshows in London, Paris, Dubai, Houston and other centres remain common. There are sound reasons for this. Capital must be pursued where it exists. But the pattern has consequences. Every time Africa’s investment conversation is exported, those foreign centres become more entrenched as the places where African opportunities are discussed. That reinforces the very gravitational pull African institutions later complain about. The long-term goal should not be to abandon international roadshows. It should be to ensure that global investors increasingly feel they must also come to Africa. Riyadh has understood that logic Saudi Arabia offers the opposite model. The Kingdom is not content simply to send delegations abroad. It is bringing the global energy industry into Riyadh. That is why the WPC gathering matters strategically. It helps concentrate ministers, CEOs, investors and media in one city. The conference becomes part of national positioning. Saudi Arabia wants executives in Riyadh. It wants deals there; it wants announcements there. It wants the city to be recognised as a global energy centre. Africa should study that strategy rather than view it only as a threat. The strongest answer to Riyadh is not merely to criticise Saudi Arabia. It is to build African platforms that generate the same institutional loyalty. A continental calendar could become economic infrastructure Africa already coordinates on issues far more complicated than conference dates. Governments negotiate trade agreements, regional blocs align economic policy. Petroleum-producing states cooperate through APPO. Development finance institutions operate across borders. There is therefore no reason the continent’s major energy institutions cannot develop a more coordinated strategic calendar. Such a system would not eliminate private events. It could simply identify a limited number of priority continental gatherings several years ahead. Governments could commit senior representation. National oil companies could reserve participation. African financial institutions could organise investment programmes around them. Corporate partners could plan sponsorship and executive attendance earlier. That would create certainty and certainty creates leverage. Events must also earn protection There is, however, another side to the argument. A conference cannot demand special treatment simply because it calls itself important. Strategic status must be earned. African events must show measurable value. How much financing was initiated, how many projects secured partners? How many government-investor meetings took place, how many licensing opportunities advanced? How many transactions announced one year actually progressed by the next? Those are the metrics that matter. The stronger the economic results, the easier it becomes for governments and companies to regard the event as indispensable. Calendar power ultimately follows economic relevance. October is an African test too It remains legitimate to question WPC’s decision to occupy virtually the same week as AEW. The overlap is real, and competition for senior delegates will be intense. But focusing only on Riyadh misses the larger lesson. Africa cannot control every international conference. It cannot order WPC to move. It cannot prevent another clash in future. What it can control is the strength of its own institutions. If AEW — or any continental platform — becomes deeply embedded in government, corporate and investor planning, competing against it becomes somebody else’s problem. That is the position Africa should seek. Not protection through complaint. Protection through relevance. The real battle is institutional habit The strongest international gatherings become powerful because attendance becomes automatic. Executives do not ask every year whether the event matters. It is already in the diary. Governments expect to participate. Investors budget for it and media organisations plan coverage. Companies organise announcements around it. Africa must build the same habit around its strongest platforms. That is the deeper lesson from the WPC–AEW clash. The most important question is no longer simply whether Riyadh crowded Africa’s calendar. It is whether Africa has made its own calendar powerful enough that doing so carries consequences. Until it does, similar clashes will keep happening. And Africa will continue asking the world to respect dates it has not yet fully institutionalised itself.

items.title: ‎Confédération AES : Le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré réaffirme son soutien aux initiatives humanitaires et de promotion du genre
items.description: ‎ ‎(Ouagadougou, 12 août 2026). Le Président du Faso, Chef de l'État, Président de la Confédération des États du Sahel, le Camarade Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, a accordé une audience, ce mercredi dans la matinée, aux ministres chargés de l'Action humanitaire et du Genre des pays de la Confédération des États du Sahel (AES). ‎Conduite par la Ministre burkinabè de la Famille et de la Solidarité, le Lieutenant-Colonel Passowendé Pélagie Kaboré, la délégation est venue rendre compte de la tenue à Ouagadougou du 2e forum humanitaire conjointement avec la réunion des ministres chargées du Genre de AES. ‎De l'urgence à la résilience ‎Au regard des défis sécuritaires et socio-économiques du Sahel, la stratégie humanitaire de l'AES doit dépasser la simple gestion de la crise immédiate pour bâtir un avenir durable, selon la porte-parole de la délégation, la Ministre de la Santé et du Développement social du Mali, Colonel-Major Assa Badiallo TOURÉ. ‎« Par rapport à l'humanitaire, il faut qu'on sorte de tout ce qui est urgence pour passer à la résilience et à des projets de relèvement pour nos populations », a-t-elle indiqué, tout en soulignant que cette orientation s’inscrit dans l'élaboration d’une feuille de route commune issue des concertations précédentes tenues à Niamey et à Bamako. ‎Lancement imminent de la Plateforme des Femmes de l'AES ‎Le volet social et inclusif est aussi dans l'agenda des ministres de la Confédération, qui s'activent pour une représentativité des femmes au Sahel. « En ce qui concerne le forum sur le Genre, il y aura le lancement de la plateforme des femmes de l'AES », a annoncé Madame Assa Badiallo Touré. ‎Réconfortées par les directives et l'engagement du Président de la Confédération AES à les accompagner, les ministres se disent confiantes quant à la concrétisation des projets de l'An 2 de la Confédération pour le bonheur de leurs populations. ‎Direction de la communication de la Présidence du Faso Minute.bf

items.title: Ukraine submits peace proposals to U.S. negotiators
items.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky on Wednesday said that Kyiv had submitted proposals to U.S. negotiators outlining a possible plan to end the war with Russia. Zelenskiy also suggested that Moscow could use next month’s parliamentary election as a pretext for launching a new mobilisation. Peace efforts have largely stalled since the outbreak of the conflict with Iran, with Ukraine continuing to push for a ceasefire after nearly four and a half years of fighting. “We have conveyed our proposals to the American side,” Zelenskiy said in his nightly video address. He said U.S. negotiators were expected to visit both Russia and Ukraine soon and added that Washington could help strengthen Ukraine’s defence capabilities. Zelensky did not disclose details of the proposals. U.S. negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner last visited Moscow in January but have yet to travel to Kyiv. Russia says it is seeking a settlement but maintains that any agreement must include Ukraine’s full withdrawal from four regions claimed by Moscow and address what it describes as the conflict’s “root causes.” The post Ukraine submits peace proposals to U.S. negotiators appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Three arrested over suspected arson that killed herbalist Dr Felix Antwi Dankwa
items.description: Three people, including the wife of a renowned herbalist, Dr Felix Antwi Dankwa, have been arrested in connection with a suspected arson incident at Kasoa in the Central Region that claimed his life. The 67-year-old herbalist, who was the Chief Executive Officer of Antwi Herbal, died after a fire gutted his residence, which also served as a clinic, on the night of Monday, August 10, 2026. Three other occupants, including his wife, escaped the blaze without injuries. Although the family has yet to officially comment on the incident, sources close to the deceased say Dr Antwi Dankwa had been involved in a marital dispute with his wife, who lived abroad. According to the source, the couple had reported to the Kasoa District Police Command earlier on Monday following allegations that the wife had changed the ownership details of some of the herbalist’s assets. The source said an altercation reportedly occurred between the couple at the police station, after which the police cautioned them and directed them to appear before a court on Tuesday, August 11. Following the fire, police officers who visited the scene arrested Dr Antwi Dankwa’s wife and two workers who also lived at the residence to assist with investigations. Sources have raised suspicion that the herbalist may have been killed before the building was set ablaze in an attempt to conceal the alleged crime. However, the circumstances surrounding his death have not been officially established. Police investigations are ongoing to determine the cause of the fire and the circumstances leading to Dr Antwi Dankwa’s death. Dr Antwi Dankwa was recently recognised by the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST) for his contribution and partnership in promoting herbal medicine.

items.title: NACOC receives IT boost to tackle emerging cyber-enabled drug trafficking
items.description: Mood Digital Services Ltd (MDSL), a technology company, has donated 50 HP laptops and other information technology equipment to the Narcotics Control Commission (NACOC) to strengthen the Commission’s IT-led and regional operations. The donation is also expected to enhance NACOC’s intelligence-gathering capabilities, particularly in efforts to detect and disrupt narcotics-related activities conducted through digital and cyber platforms. Other items presented to the Commission included an industrial printer, two servers, two 2,000VA UPS units, five projectors, a drone and drone bag, four all-in-one computers, 10 1,200VA UPS units and five iPads. Speaking at the presentation ceremony at the NACOC headquarters, the Director-General of the Commission, Major General Maxwell Obuba Mantey, thanked the management of MDSL for supporting the Commission in the discharge of its mandate. He said the equipment would improve the Commission’s operational capacity and assured that the items would be put to good use. Major General Obuba Mantey said the changing nature of illicit drug trafficking and abuse, particularly the use of cyber platforms by persons involved in the trade, had become a major concern for the Commission. He said NACOC was working to strengthen its capacity to identify and combat emerging forms of drug trafficking, including those facilitated through digital platforms. The Director-General also appealed to other corporate institutions to partner with NACOC and support efforts to address the growing threat posed by drug trafficking and abuse in Ghana. The Chief Executive Officer of Mood Digital Services Ltd, Daniel Afari, said stronger collaboration between the private sector and NACOC was necessary to enable the Commission to effectively fulfil its mandate. He said the company’s support would be sustained and extended to NACOC’s regional commands to strengthen their technological capabilities. Mr Afari also disclosed that his team would continue to partner with the Commission on its proposed mandatory drug testing exercise by providing technical and logistical support. He said the partnership forms part of MDSL’s commitment to using technology to support national efforts to combat illicit drug trafficking and abuse.

items.description: Deputy Interior Minister, Ebenezer Okletey Terlabi, has commended the 2026 Civil Service Week celebration, describing it as an important platform to highlight the contribution of the Civil Service to Ghana’s development. Mr Terlabi made the remarks when he interacted with staff of the Ministry of the Interior and its agencies at an exhibition held at the Accra Sports Stadium as part of the celebration. He said the exhibition was helping to showcase the strategic role of the Civil Service in Ghana’s sustainable development agenda while creating public awareness of government services. “The exhibition is also showcasing government’s achievements across the various Ministries and Departments. This is a positive way of creating awareness of the services being provided in the Civil Service,” he said. The Deputy Minister, accompanied by the Chief Director of the Ministry, Doreen Annan, toured exhibition stands mounted by the Ministry, the Ghana Prisons Service, Ghana National Fire Service, Narcotics Control Commission, National Commission on Small Arms and Light Weapons and other institutions. He particularly praised the Ghana Prisons Service for showcasing products made by inmates, including dresses, bags, furniture and beads. Mr Terlabi said the creativity demonstrated by the inmates reflected the importance of skills development and rehabilitation within the prison system. The 2026 Civil Service Week celebration is being organised by the Office of the Head of Civil Service on the theme: “ The Resetting Agenda for Sustainable Development in Ghana: The Civil Service’s Responsibility .” The annual celebration seeks to recognise the contribution of civil servants to national development while promoting professionalism, efficiency and patriotism in public service.

items.title: Tinubu should listen to Catholic Bishops, stop attacks — KNN
items.description: — Group says clerics echoed pains of millions of Nigerians — Backs Obi-Kwankwaso ticket for 2027 By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — The South-East chapter of the Kwankwaso National Network (KNN) has urged President Bola Ahmed Tinubu to engage Catholic bishops in constructive dialogue instead of responding to their criticism of his administration with verbal attacks. The group also called on Nigerians not to lose hope, saying a proposed Peter Obi-Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso joint ticket in the 2027 presidential election could provide an alternative to the current political order. In a statement signed by its Zonal Coordinator, Dr Ukpa Iro Ukpai, the KNN said the Catholic bishops had expressed concerns shared by many Nigerians over economic hardship, insecurity, unemployment and declining purchasing power. The group urged the Presidency to address the issues raised by the clerics rather than focus on the persons delivering the message. It said the bishops were not political opponents of the administration but religious leaders and citizens with a responsibility to speak on matters affecting the welfare and future of Nigerians. “President Tinubu should listen to the message, not attack the messenger,” the group said. According to KNN, democratic governance requires openness to criticism and opposing views, particularly when such concerns reflect the experiences of citizens. It urged the Presidency to respond to the bishops’ concerns through engagement, clarification and appropriate policy measures. The group also appealed to the President to encourage his aides and supporters to refrain from personal attacks against religious leaders and other Nigerians expressing concerns about governance. KNN called on the Presidency to invite the bishops to a constructive dialogue and consider the issues raised during such engagement. “The Bishops have done the nation a service by speaking when others may be afraid to speak. They spoke not merely for themselves, but echoed the anxieties of millions of Nigerians who are feeling the weight of the country’s present economic and social challenges,” the group stated. The South-East KNN maintained that government should remain responsive to the concerns, fears and aspirations of citizens. It called for less political rhetoric and greater focus on policies capable of improving the living conditions of Nigerians. On the 2027 election, the group expressed support for a possible Peter Obi-Kwankwaso political partnership, describing it as an opportunity for Nigerians to consider an alternative leadership direction. KNN said such a partnership could promote a shift from a consumption-driven economy to one focused more on production and economic opportunities. It also urged Nigerians to participate actively in the electoral process, reject electoral manipulation and prioritise competence and integrity when choosing leaders. The group cautioned voters against exchanging their votes for temporary material benefits, saying such incentives could not address the long-term challenges facing citizens. items.title: La Bourse de Casablanca clôture dans le vert
items.description: La Bourse de Casablanca a gagné du terrain mercredi à la clôture, son indice principal, le MASI, progressant de 0,65% à 18.825,54 points (pts). Le MASI 20, qui regroupe les 20 valeurs les plus liquides, a pris 0,27% à 1.359,54 pts et le MASI ESG, indice des entreprises ayant la meilleure notation ESG selon Moody's ESG Solutions, s'est apprécié de 1,17% à 1.387,43 pts. Contre-tendance, le MASI Mid and Small Cap, qui reflète la performance des petites et moyennes capitalisations, a reculé de 0,1% à 1.814,61 pts. Sur le plan sectoriel, les indices « Mines » (+3,66%), « Sylviculture et papier » (+3,64%) et « Services de transport » (+1,62%) ont signé les meilleures performances. À l'inverse, les secteurs « Industrie agricole » (-2,74%), « Chimie » (-1,66%) et « Télécommunications » (-0,52%) ont accusé les plus forts replis. Les échanges ont porté sur plus de 148,87 millions de dirhams (MDH), réalisés principalement sur le marché central et dominés par les transactions sur Managem (61,55 MDH), Douja Prom Addoha (9,18 MDH) et Itissalat Al-Maghrib (8,22 MDH). La capitalisation boursière a, quant à elle, dépassé 1.105,9 milliards de dirhams. Aux valeurs individuelles, Fenie Brossette (+6,67% à 390,3 DH), Zellidja S.A (+4,49% à 328 DH), Managem (+4,23% à 1.700 DH), Med Paper (+3,64% à 26,48 DH) et Involys (+2,22% à 136 DH) ont enregistré les plus fortes progressions. Les plus fortes baisses ont été accusées par IB Maroc.com (-7,83% à 55,21 DH), CMGP Group (-2,74% à 320 DH), Rebab Company (-2,51% à 93 DH), M2M Group (-2,44% à 400 DH) et Maghrebail (-2,11% à 930 DH). items.title: Court dismisses APC aspirant’s suit against Adefiranye over Ondo Reps ticket
items.description: By Dayo Johnson Akure Justice Joyce Abdulmalik of the Federal High Court, Abuja, has dismissed a suit filed by APC aspirant, Mr. Matthew Oyerinmade, challenging the emergence of Hon. Festus Ayodele Adefiranye as the party’s candidate for Ile-Oluji/Oke-Igbo/Odigbo Federal Constituency in the 2027 House of Representatives election. The case was dismissed after Oyerinmade sought to withdraw the suit “for personal reasons.” His counsel, Dr. Remi Olatubora, SAN, told the court of the plaintiff’s intention to withdraw. However, counsel to Adefiranye — Abiola Olawole, Samuel Ntibi and Daramola Martins opposed the application. They argued that issues had already been joined in the matter and the law no longer permitted a unilateral withdrawal. Ruling on the submissions, Justice Abdulmalik agreed with the defence. The Presiding judge said that “issues have been joined in this matter. I will make an order of dismissal,” she ruled. The court dismissed the suit and made no order as to cost, effectively ending Oyerinmade’s legal challenge against Adefiranye’s candidacy. The development contradicts an earlier statement by Segun Odidi of the MATO Mandate Group, which claimed the court had granted an order permitting withdrawal. Oyerinmade was among the aspirants backed by Ondo State Governor, Lucky Aiyedatiwa, who contested for the APC National Assembly ticket but lost in the primaries. A source close to the aspirant said he has concluded plans to defect to the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, where he intends to pursue the Ondo South Senatorial seat in 2027. Legal experts, however, say the manner of dismissal could have implications for any future political ambition. They noted that the judge did not allow withdrawal but dismissed the suit after upholding the defence’s argument that issues had been joined. items.title: Heirs Life Assurance nomme le pasteur Jerry Eze administrateur indépendant non exécutif
items.description: Lagos, Nigéria – 10 août 2026 – Heirs Life Assurance, la compagnie d’assurance-vie spécialisée du groupe Heirs Insurance Group, a nommé le pasteur Jerry Eze au poste d’administrateur indépendant non exécutif de son conseil d’administration, avec effet au 10 août 2026. Cette nomination renforce l’engagement de Heirs Life Assurance en faveur de l’inclusion financière et de l’accélération de l’adoption de l’assurance, en renforçant la confiance du public, l’éducation des consommateurs et la résilience financière à long terme à travers le Nigéria. Le pasteur Jerry Eze est le fondateur et pasteur principal de Streams of Joy International Ministry Malgré son statut de première économie d’Afrique, le taux de pénétration de l’assurance au Nigéria reste inférieur à 1 %, ce qui en fait l’un des plus faibles au monde. Cette situation souligne la nécessité d’élargir l’accès à la protection financière et de renforcer la confiance du public dans l’assurance. Alors que Heirs Life poursuit sa mission de rendre l’assurance accessible à tous les Nigérians, la nomination de M. Eze apporte une perspective unique en matière d’engagement communautaire, de leadership fondé sur des valeurs et d’impact sociétal à grande échelle. Le pasteur Jerry Eze est le fondateur et pasteur principal de Streams of Joy International Ministry, une organisation religieuse multinationale en pleine croissance qui compte 34 assemblées en Afrique de l’Ouest, en Afrique australe, en Europe et en Amérique du Nord. Il est également l’initiateur de New Season Prophetic Prayers and Declaration (NSPPD), l’une des plus grandes plateformes numériques de prière au monde, qui touche quotidiennement des millions de personnes. À travers son ministère et ses initiatives humanitaires, il est devenu l’une des voix les plus influentes d’Afrique, œuvrant en faveur de l’espoir, de la compassion et de la transformation des communautés. En dehors de ses activités religieuses, M. Eze est le fondateur de la Jerry Eze Foundation, une organisation philanthropique fondée sur la foi qui apporte une aide au logement et des subventions aux communautés vulnérables et défavorisées. En 2026, il a annoncé l’octroi de 1 milliard de nairas de subventions destinées à soutenir de jeunes entrepreneurs dans les secteurs de l’agriculture, des technologies et de l’industrie manufacturière, contribuant ainsi au développement des entreprises et à la création d’opportunités économiques. Avant de se consacrer à plein temps au ministère religieux, le pasteur Jerry Eze a fait carrière dans la communication pour le développement. Il a notamment travaillé comme spécialiste de la communication dans le cadre d’un programme de la Banque mondiale consacré au VIH/sida, ainsi qu’auprès du Fonds des Nations unies pour la population (UNFPA). Il est titulaire d’une licence en histoire et relations internationales de l’Abia State University et d’un diplôme de troisième cycle en administration des affaires de l’Enugu State University of Science and Technology. S’exprimant au sujet de cette nomination, Tony O. Elumelu, CFR, président du conseil d’administration de Heirs Life Assurance, a déclaré : « Le pasteur Jerry apporte une combinaison exceptionnelle d’intégrité, d’influence et de compréhension approfondie des personnes et des communautés. Alors que nous poursuivons notre mission de démocratiser l’accès à l’assurance, sa vision contribuera à renforcer la confiance des consommateurs, à approfondir l’inclusion financière et à consolider notre engagement à protéger l’avenir financier de millions de Nigérians. Nous sommes ravis de l’accueillir au sein du conseil d’administration de Heirs Life Assurance ainsi que dans la grande famille de Heirs Insurance Group. » Commentant sa nomination, le pasteur Jerry Eze a déclaré : « Je suis honoré de rejoindre le conseil d’administration de Heirs Life Assurance à un moment déterminant pour le secteur de l’assurance. La sécurité financière permet aux particuliers, aux familles et aux entreprises de poursuivre leurs aspirations avec davantage de confiance et de résilience. Je me réjouis de travailler avec le conseil d’administration et la direction afin de faire progresser la mission de l’entreprise : rendre l’assurance plus accessible, plus pertinente et plus bénéfique pour chaque Nigérian. » Tony O. Elumelu, CFR, président du conseil d’administration de Heirs Life Assurance Heirs Life Assurance est devenue l’une des principales compagnies d’assurance-vie spécialisées du Nigéria. Elle figure au 7e rang du classement du Financial Times des entreprises à la croissance la plus rapide en Afrique. Elle fait partie des trois activités d’assurance de Heirs Holdings, l’un des principaux groupes d’investissement panafricains, qui détient des participations dans 24 pays et sur quatre continents. Grâce à une présence numérique omnicanale et à un réseau d’agences physiques réparties à travers le pays, Heirs Life continue de redéfinir l’assurance-vie grâce à l’innovation, à des solutions centrées sur le client et à son engagement à rendre la protection financière accessible à tous les Nigérians. Heirs Insurance Group, qui regroupe Heirs Life Assurance, Heirs General Insurance et Heirs Insurance Brokers, sert collectivement plus de 3 millions de personnes, directement et indirectement. Le groupe joue un rôle moteur dans l’inclusion financière et le développement de l’assurance numérique au Nigéria, concrétisant ainsi sa mission de démocratiser l’accès à l’assurance. items.title: Millions of people in Iceland and Spain set for 'event of the century' eclipse
items.description: Millions of people gathered in Iceland and northern Spain to witness Europe’s first total solar eclipse in 27 years on Wednesday, with Spanish officials warning people to avoid areas where a heatwave has raised the risk of wildfires. Authorities were expecting up to 6 million visitors in mostly rural areas within the eclipse’s path across the north of Spain and the Balearic Islands, said Juan Cruz, Spain’s Secretary of State for Science. “I hope that tonight will see the emergence of a wonderful generation of astrophysicists,” he said. “It’s such a special moment.” The eclipse will be quickly followed by the sunset in Spain, making the event particularly alluring. Police, planes, and helicopters are on standby The uncanny sensation when day briefly turns into twilight and some animals fall quiet as the moon passes directly between Earth and the Sun was often treated as an omen in the past, a cosmic struggle or a sign of divine power. Frenchman Leyssalle Anthony, 39, prepares a telescope to view the total solar eclipse from the beach, in Arija, Spain, August 12, 2026. — Reuters Now, Spain sees it as a chance to showcase seldom-visited regions and draw tourists away from its overcrowded beach resorts, while also rolling out a massive police operation and public safety campaign to prevent them from causing wildfires. Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska told reporters 25,000 police officers had been assigned to guarantee security around the eclipse observation while nearly 100 planes and helicopters were also being deployed. He called on citizens to follow the eclipse from the hundreds of observation points set up by authorities and abide by the restrictions set up around some parks. “Let’s not forget that the wildfire risk is very high; it’s extreme due to high temperatures,” he said. Lola Guerreiro spent the night in the mountains near Arco de las Salinas in eastern Spain, home to Galactica Europe’s largest educational astronomy centre as well as the Javalambre observatory, after making the long drive from Extremadura to view the eclipse. People walk out of a portable planetarium during an eclipse watch party on the day of a total solar eclipse in Buitrago del Lozoya, Spain, August 12, 2026. — Reuters “Watching a total solar eclipse has been a dream of mine for many, many years, and I didn’t want to miss the chance to experience it, even though it meant a seven-hour journey,” she said. Sergio, a 60-year-old Italian, had made the trek in a camping van with his family to Arija in northern Spain. “I do feel a little emotional. Yes, because I know I won’t have another chance in my life to see an eclipse, a phenomenon like this,” he said. The Iberian Peninsula last saw a total solar eclipse in 1912. It is set to experience another one on August 2, 2027, and an annular eclipse in January 2028, completing the so-called “Iberian Eclipse Trio.” Eclipse fever in the land of sagas In Iceland’s capital Reykjavik, glasses to allow people to look at the phenomenon without damaging their eyes have been sold out for days as the Nordic country of roughly 400,000 people expects to welcome up to 80,000 visitors. A narrow path of totality will reach Iceland’s westernmost coast at about 5:44pm (1744 GMT), before the moon’s shadow races east. People lie down inside a portable planetarium during an eclipse watch party on the day of a total solar eclipse in Buitrago del Lozoya, Spain, August 12, 2026. — Reuters Totality will last up to 2 minutes and 13 seconds in the far west, though most cities will see shorter periods of darkness. Authorities have warned of heavy traffic and urged viewers to arrive early. Singer Bjork was due to perform a DJ set at an eclipse-themed event south of Reykjavik. US space agency Nasa plans to fly a high-altitude WB-57 aircraft from Iceland to follow the moon’s shadow, and Nasa-funded teams will launch balloons to study how the sudden darkness and cooling affect the lower atmosphere. “This is a once-in-a-lifetime experience,” said Karen Williams, 51, who was visiting from Britain. “I love the outdoors, and so I wanted to come and see the eclipse and just experience it.” Angela Cordoba reacts as she wears virtual reality goggles next to her grandchildren, Gadea, 3, and Giulia, 6, as they attend an eclipse watch party on the day of a total solar eclipse in Buitrago del Lozoya, Spain, August 12, 2026. “Although I do hear, probably in the UK where I’ve come from… they’re going to get a better view of it than us here tonight.” Skies over Iceland were overcast on Wednesday with the Icelandic Met office predicting clouds and rain for much of the path of the eclipse, adding that the best chances of breaks in the solid cover were expected in the northwest of the country. Aside from casual observers, the event also draws “eclipse chasers”, enthusiasts who crisscross the globe to be in the path of totality whenever an eclipse occurs. Gordon Telepun, a retired plastic surgeon and amateur astronomer from the US who has photographed six total eclipses, said he would watch from the island of Mallorca because Spain checked all the boxes for eclipse chasers.

Osun Election: APC chieftain urges peace, responsible political engagement
items.description: By Dapo Akinrefon OSOGBO — A chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Osun State, Mr Olatunbosun Oyintiloye, has urged political actors and stakeholders to shun violence and promote peaceful engagement ahead of the August 15 governorship election. Oyintiloye made the call on Wednesday while addressing journalists during an empowerment programme for informal workers at his campaign office in Ibokun, Obokun Local Government Area of the state. He stressed that the APC remained committed to peaceful political activities and appealed to stakeholders and members of the public to promote tolerance and responsible engagement before, during and after the election. The programme attracted informal workers, including barbers, hairdressers, fumigators, welders, textile workers, members of the National Union of Tailors and Electrical Workers, market men and women, commercial motorcyclists and members of the Nigeria Automobile Technicians Association (NATA). Members of non-indigenous communities, including Igede, Idoma and Tiv residents from Benue State living in Obokun Local Government Area, also attended the event. Oyintiloye said the empowerment programme was part of his efforts to support hardworking residents and strengthen grassroots participation in governance. He urged the beneficiaries to see the initiative as an expression of his commitment to the welfare of ordinary citizens, particularly people whose livelihoods depend on their daily businesses and skills. He also urged the participants to return to their communities and support the APC candidate, Asiwaju Munirudeen Bola Oyebamiji, in the election. Oyintiloye said an Oyebamiji-led administration would prioritise inclusive governance, economic empowerment, skills development and improved opportunities for workers in the informal sector. He stressed that every segment of society would be given attention under the proposed administration. A community leader, Bishop Michael Adewale, commended the initiative, describing it as a demonstration of grassroots-oriented politics and concern for the welfare of residents. He urged the beneficiaries to remain united and peaceful before, during and after the election, stressing that political differences should not be allowed to damage existing relationships in the communities. Speaking on behalf of artisans and other informal workers, Mr Tijani Bello expressed appreciation for the support extended to them during the civic engagement programme. Bello said artisans constituted a significant part of the grassroots economy and deserved access to empowerment programmes, skills development, financial support, infrastructure and better economic opportunities. He assured the organisers that the artisans would take the message of the programme back to their communities and mobilise support for Oyebamiji and the APC. items.title: Singer Niniola returns with new single ‘O Du Mi’ after husband’s death
items.description: Afro-house singer, Niniola Apata, is set to release a new single “O Du Mi”, months after the death of her husband, Michael Ndika. The song, scheduled for release on Aug. 14 will be her first major musical project since Ndika’s passing in May 2026. Ndika, who was the CEO of NaijaReview and also served as her manager, was married to the singer for 13 years. Niniola shared emotional posts on social media describing her grief, including messages such as “God took him” and “My husband died,” later referring to him as her “best friend, confidant, pillar, business partner and husband”. The singer said the new single reflects a deeply personal phase in her life, capturing themes of love, loss and emotional healing. “Some feelings are too deep for words. So I put them in a song,” she wrote while sharing a preview of the track. Despite the loss, she has gradually returned to public engagements, including live performances and appearances, and was recently spotted at her younger sister Teniola Apata’s album launch. Ahead of one of her performances, Niniola said returning to music remained emotionally challenging, adding: “There are no words for a moment like this, but I know he’d want me to keep singing, to keep showing up, and to keep sharing the gift we’ve always believed in.” Her return with “O Du Mi” is expected to mark a new phase in her career as she continues to build on her Afro-house sound. Niniola, known for songs such as “Maradona” and “Designer,” remains one of Nigeria’s leading Afro-house artistes, blending traditional African sounds with contemporary music. (NAN) The post Singer Niniola returns with new single ‘O Du Mi’ after husband’s death appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Niger Flooding: Northern senators seek permanent solution beyond emergency response
items.description: — Call for coordinated action by FG, state government — Commiserate with families affected by disaster By Henry Umoru ABUJA — Senators from the 19 Northern states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), under the aegis of the Northern Senators Forum (NSF), have called for a permanent and coordinated solution to recurring flooding in Shiroro, Minna and other communities in Niger State. The lawmakers said the situation required more than annual emergency responses, urging the Federal and Niger State governments to adopt long-term measures to prevent loss of lives and property. The call followed recent flooding in parts of Minna, Chanchaga, Bosso and Shiroro Local Government Areas of the state. In a statement issued on Wednesday, Chairman of the NSF, Senator Abdulaziz Musa Yar’Adua (APC, Katsina Central), commiserated with the government and people of Niger State, particularly families affected by the disaster. The forum sympathised with families who lost loved ones, homes, farms, businesses and sources of livelihood, while expressing concern over the hardship faced by displaced residents. The senators acknowledged the response of the National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA) and the Niger State Emergency Management Agency (NSEMA) in assessing and documenting the impact of the flooding. However, they noted that flooding in Shiroro and other riverine communities had become a recurring problem that required both immediate intervention and long-term planning. The forum urged the Federal and state governments, in collaboration with local authorities, to ensure prompt distribution of relief materials to verified victims and provide temporary shelters with basic healthcare and sanitation facilities. It also called for the deployment of emergency evacuation teams and early-warning systems in flood-prone communities ahead of the peak of the rainy season. The senators urged residents to heed safety advisories and avoid construction on waterways and other flood-prone areas. For the long term, the forum called for the development of a Shiroro Flood Management Master Plan. According to the senators, the plan should include a scientifically determined flood-buffer operating strategy for the Shiroro, Kainji and Jebba dams, as well as a permanent flood forecasting and early-warning system supported by trained local volunteers downstream. The forum also proposed a comprehensive floodplain resettlement programme that would provide planned settlements, compensation and livelihood support for affected residents. It further called for an independent technical review of dam operations, reservoir capacity and spillway performance in view of changing climate conditions, to determine how future water releases could be better managed. The senators cited the 2025 Mokwa flooding and a 2025 vulnerability study indicating that 32 per cent of Shiroro Local Government Area was highly prone to flooding as evidence of the need for urgent action. They said infrastructure interventions, including road and drainage repairs, should be integrated into a broader water-resource and environmental management framework addressing deforestation, inadequate drainage and unregulated development along riverbanks. The forum assured the people of Niger State of its commitment to advocating appropriate budgetary provisions and legislative support aimed at reducing the impact of flooding and preventing avoidable disasters. It also called on federal and state agencies, traditional and community leaders and residents to work together to protect lives and strengthen resilience against future flooding. The senators prayed for comfort for bereaved families, strength for displaced residents and wisdom for authorities working to find lasting solutions to the recurring flooding. items.title: Heirs Life Assurance nomme le pasteur Jerry Eze administrateur indépendant non exécutif
items.description: G – D : Tony Elumelu, Président du conseil d’administration de Heirs Life Assurance ; Pasteur Jerry Eze, administrateur de Heirs Life Assurance Lagos, Nigéria – 10 août 2026 – Heirs Life Assurance, la compagnie d’assurance-vie spécialisée du groupe Heirs Insurance Group, a nommé le pasteur Jerry Eze au poste d’administrateur indépendant non exécutif de son conseil d’administration, avec effet au 10 août 2026. Cette nomination renforce l’engagement de Heirs Life Assurance en faveur de l’inclusion financière et de l’accélération de l’adoption de l’assurance, en renforçant la confiance du public, l’éducation des consommateurs et la résilience financière à long terme à travers le Nigéria. Malgré son statut de première économie d’Afrique, le taux de pénétration de l’assurance au Nigéria reste inférieur à 1 %, ce qui en fait l’un des plus faibles au monde. Cette situation souligne la nécessité d’élargir l’accès à la protection financière et de renforcer la confiance du public dans l’assurance. Alors que Heirs Life poursuit sa mission de rendre l’assurance accessible à tous les Nigérians, la nomination de M. Eze apporte une perspective unique en matière d’engagement communautaire, de leadership fondé sur des valeurs et d’impact sociétal à grande échelle. Le pasteur Jerry Eze est le fondateur et pasteur principal de Streams of Joy International Ministry, une organisation religieuse multinationale en pleine croissance qui compte 34 assemblées en Afrique de l’Ouest, en Afrique australe, en Europe et en Amérique du Nord. Il est également l’initiateur de New Season Prophetic Prayers and Declaration (NSPPD), l’une des plus grandes plateformes numériques de prière au monde, qui touche quotidiennement des millions de personnes. À travers son ministère et ses initiatives humanitaires, il est devenu l’une des voix les plus influentes d’Afrique, œuvrant en faveur de l’espoir, de la compassion et de la transformation des communautés. En dehors de ses activités religieuses, M. Eze est le fondateur de la Jerry Eze Foundation, une organisation philanthropique fondée sur la foi qui apporte une aide au logement et des subventions aux communautés vulnérables et défavorisées. En 2026, il a annoncé l’octroi de 1 milliard de nairas de subventions destinées à soutenir de jeunes entrepreneurs dans les secteurs de l’agriculture, des technologies et de l’industrie manufacturière, contribuant ainsi au développement des entreprises et à la création d’opportunités économiques. Avant de se consacrer à plein temps au ministère religieux, le pasteur Jerry Eze a fait carrière dans la communication pour le développement. Il a notamment travaillé comme spécialiste de la communication dans le cadre d’un programme de la Banque mondiale consacré au VIH/sida, ainsi qu’auprès du Fonds des Nations unies pour la population (UNFPA). Il est titulaire d’une licence en histoire et relations internationales de l’Abia State University et d’un diplôme de troisième cycle en administration des affaires de l’Enugu State University of Science and Technology. S’exprimant au sujet de cette nomination, Tony O. Elumelu, CFR, président du conseil d’administration de Heirs Life Assurance, a déclaré : « Le pasteur Jerry apporte une combinaison exceptionnelle d’intégrité, d’influence et de compréhension approfondie des personnes et des communautés. Alors que nous poursuivons notre mission de démocratiser l’accès à l’assurance, sa vision contribuera à renforcer la confiance des consommateurs, à approfondir l’inclusion financière et à consolider notre engagement à protéger l’avenir financier de millions de Nigérians. Nous sommes ravis de l’accueillir au sein du conseil d’administration de Heirs Life Assurance ainsi que dans la grande famille de Heirs Insurance Group. » Commentant sa nomination, le pasteur Jerry Eze a déclaré : « Je suis honoré de rejoindre le conseil d’administration de Heirs Life Assurance à un moment déterminant pour le secteur de l’assurance. La sécurité financière permet aux particuliers, aux familles et aux entreprises de poursuivre leurs aspirations avec davantage de confiance et de résilience. Je me réjouis de travailler avec le conseil d’administration et la direction afin de faire progresser la mission de l’entreprise : rendre l’assurance plus accessible, plus pertinente et plus bénéfique pour chaque Nigérian. » Heirs Life Assurance est devenue l’une des principales compagnies d’assurance-vie spécialisées du Nigéria. Elle figure au 7e rang du classement du Financial Times des entreprises à la croissance la plus rapide en Afrique. Elle fait partie des trois activités d’assurance de Heirs Holdings, l’un des principaux groupes d’investissement panafricains, qui détient des participations dans 24 pays et sur quatre continents. Grâce à une présence numérique omnicanale et à un réseau d’agences physiques réparties à travers le pays, Heirs Life continue de redéfinir l’assurance-vie grâce à l’innovation, à des solutions centrées sur le client et à son engagement à rendre la protection financière accessible à tous les Nigérians. Heirs Insurance Group, qui regroupe Heirs Life Assurance, Heirs General Insurance et Heirs Insurance Brokers, sert collectivement plus de 3 millions de personnes, directement et indirectement. Le groupe joue un rôle moteur dans l’inclusion financière et le développement de l’assurance numérique au Nigéria, concrétisant ainsi sa mission de démocratiser l’accès à l’assurance. items.title: Burkina | Caravane de la Paix « Graines de Cohésion » : Le dialogue devient le terreau de la résilience
items.description: L’Association Jeunes Faiseurs de Paix a posé ses valises ce mercredi 12 août 2026 dans l’Arrondissement 11 de Ouagadougou pour la huitième étape de sa Caravane de la Paix. Une initiative lancée en novembre 2025 pour semer les graines du vivre-ensemble dans un contexte national marqué par des défis sécuritaires et sociaux. La cérémonie a été marquée par l’installation officielle d’une Cellule de la Paix, destinée à pérenniser le dialogue au sein des quartiers. C'est partie pour la huitième étape de la Caravane de la Paix « Graines de Cohésion ». Portée par l’Association Jeunes Faiseurs de Paix, cette caravane, lancée en novembre 2025, sillonne les différents arrondissements de la capitale pour rappeler aux populations que la paix est l’affaire de tous. Le PDS Marou Yaméogo saluant l’importance de cette rencontre… Dans son discours d’ouverture, le président de la Délégation spéciale de l’Arrondissement 11, Marou Yaméogo, a salué l’importance de cette rencontre. « Notre pays traverse une période particulière de son histoire. Les défis auxquels nous sommes confrontés exigent de chacun de nous davantage de responsabilité, de solidarité et de patriotisme. La cohésion sociale n'est pas une question secondaire. Elle constitue l'un des fondements de notre résilience collective », a-t-il planté le décor. Le parrain de la caravane, El Hadj Sayouba Traoré, dont l’accompagnement constant a été salué par les organisateurs, incarne selon eux la conviction que chaque citoyen peut contribuer, à son niveau, à l’édification d’un Burkina Faso uni. La cérémonie a également été l’occasion d’installer officiellement une Cellule de la Paix au sein de l’arrondissement. Pour Marou Yaméogo, cette structure doit devenir « un cadre permanent de dialogue, d'écoute et de sensibilisation, capable de contribuer à la prévention des tensions et au renforcement du vivre-ensemble ». Pour Hermann Guingané, la paix se construit lorsque nous choisissons l'écoute plutôt que les préjugés Le président de l’Association Jeunes Faiseurs de Paix, Hermann Guingané, a exprimé sa gratitude aux autorités locales pour leur accueil chaleureux. Il a insisté sur la philosophie qui anime cette tournée citoyenne : « La paix se construit lorsque nous nous respectons malgré nos différences. Elle se construit lorsque nous privilégions le dialogue à la division ». Pour Hermann Guingané, la paix se construit lorsque nous choisissons l'écoute plutôt que les préjugés. En citant un proverbe africain, « Une seule main ne peut pas attacher un fagot », le président de l’Association Jeunes Faiseurs de Paix a lancé un appel à l’engagement collectif pour préserver l’unité nationale. Un aperçu des participants Cette huitième étape ne se limite pas à une simple visite protocolaire. Elle marque une volonté affirmée de renforcer les liens entre les communautés en impliquant toutes les forces vives : représentants des confessions religieuses, leaders coutumiers, associations de jeunes et organisations de femmes. Les échanges ont permis de rappeler que la paix se construit au quotidien, dans les familles, les lieux de culte et les quartiers, loin des seules grandes décisions institutionnelles. Lire aussi : Burkina : Religieux et coutumiers se penchent sur la création d’un cadre de dialogue interreligieux Minute.bf

items.title: Osun Poll: Police, military, INEC don’t belong to APC — Atiku
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — Former Vice President and presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, yesterday warned the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), security agencies and the Federal Government against using state institutions to tilt the Osun governorship election in favour of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC). Atiku described the poll as a critical test of Nigeria’s democratic credentials, warning that the scale and posture of security deployment around the election risked making a civil democratic exercise look like a military operation. Speaking at the ADC National Youth Leadership Summit in Abuja, he said the conduct of the Osun election would send a strong signal about Nigeria’s readiness to deliver credible elections ahead of the next general election. “Elections are civil engagements, not military operations. Ballot papers are not bullets. Voters are not enemy combatants. Opposition members are not insurgents,” he said. Atiku questioned why such overwhelming security capacity was being deployed for an election when terrorists, kidnappers and bandits continue to attack communities and kill Nigerians. He also cautioned INEC against any attempt to frustrate voters or compromise the integrity of the process through technical failures, unexplained delays or opaque handling of results. The former vice president demanded the timely arrival of electoral materials, unhindered voting, honest counting and transparent transmission of results. “The police belong to Nigeria. The military belongs to Nigeria. INEC belongs to the Nigerian people. None of them belongs to the APC,” he declared. Atiku said the eyes of Nigerians and the international community would be on Osun, urging all institutions involved in the election to allow voters to freely determine the outcome. “The world is watching Osun. Nigerians are watching. History is taking notes. Let the people vote. Let every vote count. And let the will of the people prevail,” Atiku said. The ADC presidential candidate also returned to the controversy surrounding the Chicago State University certificate President Bola Tinubu submitted to INEC, demanding clarification of what he described as discrepancies in documents linked to the certificate. Atiku said the certificate submitted to INEC reportedly bears June 22, 1979, while another document produced in connection with Chicago State University records bears June 27, 1979. He also pointed to reported differences in the signatures and description of the degree. He questioned the appearance on documents dated 1979 of names or signatures associated with university officials whose tenures reportedly began years later, asking whether replacement certificates were subsequently produced and, if so, who authorised them. Atiku cited Section 137(1)(j) of the Constitution, which provides for disqualification where a presidential candidate has presented a forged certificate to INEC, arguing that the precise document submitted to the electoral commission should be authenticated. “Who produced the certificate Tinubu submitted to INEC? When was it produced? Who authorised it? Why does it differ from the other version, and does Chicago State University authenticate the exact document submitted to INEC?” he asked. He argued that the standard expected of an ordinary Nigerian seeking employment should not be lowered for someone seeking the country’s highest political office. “If a young Nigerian would be required to explain such discrepancies before getting an ordinary job, why should the man seeking Nigeria’s highest job be exempt from the same standard?” Atiku asked. On youth participation, Atiku pledged that at least 30 per cent of legislative candidates under his political programme would be below 40, with a significant number below 30. He urged young Nigerians to turn their frustration into organised political participation rather than stopping at social media activism. “Anger is not an organisation. A hashtag is not an organisation,” Atiku said, urging young Nigerians to move beyond online expressions of frustration and take an active role in shaping the country’s political future The post Osun Poll: Police, military, INEC don’t belong to APC — Atiku appeared first on Vanguard News .
